# ARNAV Lab Discord Simulation

Welcome to the ARNAV Lab Discord Simulation project.

> **Note:** This is a team project built for CSC 492 (Senior Design) at NC State
> University — ARNAV Lab, Team 33, Spring 2026. It is showcased here on my
> personal account. Full credit to the team: McKoy Graham, Jackson Oliver,
> Garrett Graham, Garrison Lamb, Morgan Sawyer, and Nathan Chacko.
> Original repository: `ncstate-csc-sdc/2026Spring-Team33-ARNAV`.

## Development Setup Guide

Prerequisites:

- [Node.js 24](https://nodejs.org/en)
- [Docker](https://www.docker.com/)

### 1. Building

After cloning this repository, make sure you are in the root of the project and run `npm install`.

### 2. Discord Bot Setup

1. Create a [Discord](https://discord.com) account.
2. Create a new application in the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications).
3. In the app settings, open the "Installation" tab. In the "Installation Contexts" section, make sure only "Guild Install" is selected. Click "Save Changes".
4. Still on the "Installation" page, in the "Default Install Settings" section, in "Scopes", add "bot".
5. Add "Administrator" to the "Permissions".
6. Open the "OAuth2" tab. In the "Redirects" section, click "Add Redirect" and enter the following URL: `http://localhost:3000/auth/discord/callback`
7. Open the "Bot" tab. In the "Privileged Gateway Intents" section, enable the following: "Server Members Intent", "Message Content Intent".

### 3. Discord Server Setup

1. Create a new Discord server.
2. In the Discord Developer Portal app settings, open the "Installation" tab. Copy the installation link in the "Install Link" section.
3. Open the link in your browser. Select the server you just created.

### 4. Environment Variables

In each `apps/*` sub-project, duplicate the `.env.example` file and rename it to `.env`. You can leave the keys at their default values except for the following:

- In `apps/server`:
  - `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`: Discord Application ID found in the Discord Developer Portal "General Information" tab.
  - `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`: Discord "Client Secret" found in the "OAuth2" tab.
  - `OLLAMA_URL`: A link to an Ollama server. Until May 2026 you can use this: `http://eb2-2208-aw01.csc.ncsu.edu`
  - `STABLE_DIFFUSION_URL`: A link to a Stable Diffusion server / API.
- In `apps/discord-transport`:
  - `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`: Discord Application ID found in the Discord Developer Portal "General Information" tab.
  - `DISCORD_API_TOKEN`: Discord "Token" found in the "Bot" tab. **This is not the same as the client secret from the server!**
- In `apps/bot`:
  - `OLLAMA_URL`: A link to an Ollama server. Until May 2026 you can use this: `http://eb2-2208-aw01.csc.ncsu.edu`

### 5. Test Database Initialization

We need to bootstrap the database so you can log in to the dashboard.

1. Start the development server by running `docker compose up --build`
2. In Discord, in the bottom left corner, open "User Settings". Scroll the navigation sidebar all the way down and open the "Advanced" tab. Enable "Developer Mode".
3. Click on your username in the bottom left corner and press the "Copy User ID" button.
4. (Make sure the server is running) `cd` into `apps/server` and run the command: `npm run dev:test-db YOUR_DISCORD_USER_ID`. Replace `YOUR_DISCORD_USER_ID` with the ID you just copied.

This will create an empty world and an admin user with your Discord user ID.

You can now log in to the dashboard at [http://localhost:80](http://localhost:80).

## Running

To run the application, use:

```
docker compose up --build
```

Pass `--watch` to this command if you want the server to restart when code changes.

Running this command for the first time might take a couple minutes.

You should now be able to access the dashboard by navigating to [http://localhost:80](http://localhost:80).

## Testing

To run the test suite, use:

```
docker compose --profile test up
```
